The deploy workflow used a `workflow_run` trigger chained off CI completion. While this was functioning correctly, it adds unnecessary indirection. The actual reason the latest changes hadn't deployed is that PR #80 was merged into a feature branch (`copilot/add-public-page-for-meeting-minutes`), not into `main` — so no push to `main` occurred and no deployment was triggered. PR #78 (which targets `main`) still needs to be merged to deploy those changes.

This PR simplifies the deploy trigger as a minor improvement:

- Replace `workflow_run` trigger with direct `push: branches: ['main']`
- Remove the `if` guard on `workflow_run.conclusion` (no longer applicable)

The deploy workflow already runs its own full `npm ci` + `npm run build`, so it doesn't depend on CI artifacts — a failed build still prevents deployment. CI continues to run independently as the PR quality gate.

```yaml
# Before: indirect trigger via CI workflow
on:
  workflow_run:
    workflows: ['CI - Build and Test']
    types: [completed]
    branches: ['main']

# After: direct trigger
on:
  push:
    branches: ['main']
```

author: mersad-moghaddam
body:
### Motivation

- Move the codebase to a production-oriented Hexagonal (Ports & Adapters) architecture to improve testability and separation of concerns.
- Introduce a reliable asynchronous alert flow (outbox) and safer worker/HTTP behaviour (SSRF protections, API key auth, scheduler/worker tuning).
- Replace the legacy mono-repo service/repository layers with clear domain, application and adapter boundaries and provide a lightweight admin frontend.

### Description

- Rearranged project layout and introduced domain, ports, application and adapters folders, including `internal/domain`, `internal/domain/ports`, `internal/application`, `internal/adapters/*` and `internal/platform/*` to implement Hexagonal architecture.
- Added a MySQL-backed `mysql.Store` implementing domain ports, an `outbox_events` table and migrations under `db/migrations` with `ApplyMigrations` runner in `internal/platform/storage` and updated `docker-compose.yml` to load migrations on startup.
- Implemented `application.Service` as the use-case layer and rewired the HTTP server (`internal/platform/httpserver`) to use an API key middleware (`internal/adapters/inbound/http/middleware.go`) and serve a new simple SPA frontend under `frontend/`.
- Refactored the worker processor to support batched `ListDue` enqueueing, added outbox dispatch task handling, improved monitor evaluation (`evaluate`, TLS/keyword/http checks), added SSRF and private-IP guards (`validateTarget`), and introduced a pluggable `Notifier` adapter.

### Testing

- Ran unit tests for domain policies in `internal/domain` via `go test ./internal/domain -v` and they passed.
- Ran the new worker unit test in `internal/worker` via `go test ./internal/worker -v` to validate SSRF blocking and it passed.
- A full `go test ./...` was exercised on the modified packages and the added tests succeeded.

body:
Split sandbox pool initialization into two phases so pre-warming doesn't block server startup.

## Changes

### `src/server/agent/sandbox-pool.ts`
Split `init()` into:
- **`init()`** — Synchronous essentials (detect branch, ensure dirs, kill previous containers)
- **`warmup()`** — Background pre-warming (clean stale dirs, create spare containers)

### `src/server/server.ts`
Call `sandboxPool.warmup()` fire-and-forget after `init()`, so session restore and server listen proceed while containers warm up. Restored sandboxed sessions use the existing on-demand creation fallback in `claim()`.

## Summary
- Corrects UI layout issues and hardens input validation for payments
- Reworks RTP-driven logic and payout caps across several games to improve balance stability
- sanitizes admin wallet inputs before server requests to TON services
- Minor visual tweaks to improve responsiveness and consistency across cards

## Changes
### Frontend
- public/script.js
  - Relax TON wallet validation: trim input, remove newline characters, and require non-empty address with a reasonable length instead of strict regex validation
  - Improve error messaging when recipient wallet is not configured
- public/style.css
  - Reduce mine-card max width from 260px to 240px for better layout on smaller screens
  - Adjust aspect-ratio values (1.05) across several UI elements to improve responsiveness and visual consistency

### Backend
- server.js
  - Spin /api/spin: introduce stricter, RTP-informed caps; cap actualWin to betAmount * 3 when not in free spins; refine feature frequency controls
  - Mine /api/mine: reduce MINE_BLOCK_MULTS; adjust MINE_BLOCK_MULTS and MINE_BLOCK_WEIGHTS; update chest multipliers and expected value for more balanced rewards; apply a hard cap on total win per spin
  - Plinko /api/plinko: adjust RTP-based loss chances to tighten win distribution
  - Duck /api/duck: implement RTP-driven loss chances and cap total winnings to keep payouts within reasonable bounds
  - Upgrade /api/upgrade: lower max payout relative to bet and adjust win probability with a more conservative cap
  - Check deposit /api/check_deposit: sanitize admin wallet address before querying TON Center (removing newline characters)
  - General: introduce and rely on sanitized address inputs to prevent malformed requests

### Validation & Safety
- Added address sanitization in server endpoints that contact external TON services to reduce risk from malformed or injected inputs
- Implemented tighter payout caps across games to prevent excessive wins per spin and improve balance integrity

## Test plan
- UI and layout
  - Open game lobby and verify cards render correctly with new max-width and aspect-ratio values across desktop and mobile sizes
  - Attempt payments with valid and invalid/empty recipient addresses to ensure new messages and validations appear as expected
- Payments flow
  - Trigger payWithTonConnect with valid and invalid addresses; confirm proper toast messages and lack of incorrect requests
- RTP and payout behavior (manual/runbook testing)
  - Spin: set various RTP targets and verify that max spin win does not exceed betAmount * 3 (except free-spin scenarios) and that probability behavior aligns with new logic
  - Mine: observe reduced multiplier effects and chest bonus behavior; verify total win is capped per spin as implemented
  - Plinko: test different RTP values and verify bucket outcomes follow updated loss/win logic
  - Duck: test losing vs. winning paths under different RTP targets and ensure winnings stay within cap limits
  - Upgrade: test conversion logic and caps for wins; ensure payout cannot exceed defined bound
- Deposit check endpoint
  - Call /api/check_deposit with sample admin wallet values containing stray newline characters; ensure requests are formed with clean addresses

## Notes
- Some changes adjust game balance mechanics to align with RTP-based constraints. If you rely on exact historical payout rates for compliance or audits, validate these changes in a staging environment before promotion to production.
- No UI/UX assets were removed; visual tweaks are sizing-oriented to improve consistency across devices.

body:
• *Repo:* `dheerajyadav1714/ci_cd`
• *File:* `src/bug.py`
• *Summary:* The pipeline failed due to an unhandled `ZeroDivisionError` in `src/bug.py` caused by division by zero.
• *Root Cause:* The `divide` function in `src/bug.py` does not include any validation or error handling for a zero denominator. When `print(divide(10, 0))` is executed, it attempts to perform `10 / 0`, which immediately raises a `ZeroDivisionError`. This unhandled exception causes the Python script to terminate abruptly, leading to the Jenkins pipeline failure.
• *Suggested Fix:*
```python
def divide(a, b):
    if b == 0:
        print("Error: Cannot divide by zero!")
        return None  # Return None or raise a ValueError for invalid input
    return a / b

# The original call site is modified to handle the potential None return
result = divide(10, 0)
if result is not None:
    print(result)
```
• *Severity:* High
• *Fix Confidence:* 95%

### Motivation
- The lecture UI previously relied on exact string matches against `seg.formulas[].latex` to replace math, which failed when the source `display_text` contained extra whitespace/newlines or when delimiters were omitted in the `formulas` entries.  
- The displayed/textual content for lecture segments should be taken from `seg.text`/`seg.display_text` for visual rendering rather than falling back to `seg.spoken_text` first.

### Description
- Updated `renderSegmentContent` in `frontend/public/js/app.js` to prefer `seg.text || seg.display_text || seg.spoken_text` as the source of display text.  
- Replaced brittle formula-matching logic with delimiter-based extraction: the function now scans the segment text for `$$...$$` (display math) and `$...$` (inline math) using regular expressions, replaces them with safe placeholders, and restores them after HTML escaping.  
- When KaTeX is available the restored placeholders are rendered with `katex.renderToString(...)` into `<span>` elements (classes `lecture-formula-block`/`lecture-formula`), and when KaTeX is unavailable the code falls back to the escaped raw LaTeX string.

### Testing
- Ran `node --check frontend/public/js/app.js` and the check completed without syntax errors.

author: dcccrypto
body:
## P0 — Mainnet deposit form not showing after CREATE TRADING ACCOUNT

### Root Cause
`buildLayoutV1M2()` set `acctOwnerOff: ACCT_OWNER_OFF` (184), but V1M2 uses 312-byte accounts (same struct as V_ADL) where the owner pubkey is at offset **192** due to `reserved_pnl` growing from u64 to u128 (PERC-8267).

### Symptoms
- `parseAllAccounts()` on V1M2 mainnet slabs reads 8 bytes of `matcher_context` tail as the owner pubkey
- Wallet lookup fails silently → deposit form never appears after account creation
- Affected: all V1M2 mainnet markets (323312 byte medium slabs on program ESa89R5)

### Fix
One-line change: `acctOwnerOff: ACCT_OWNER_OFF` → `acctOwnerOff: V_ADL_ACCT_OWNER_OFF` in `buildLayoutV1M2()`.

### Verification
- All 652 tests pass
- TypeScript clean (`tsc --noEmit`)
- On-chain slab probing confirms V1M2 medium (323312 bytes) now detects `acctOwnerOff=192`
- V1M (248-byte accounts) correctly keeps `acctOwnerOff=184` — no regression

### Impact
Critical 1-line fix. After merge, `packages/core` in percolator-launch picks this up via workspace link → deposit form should work.

author: copilot
body:
`AchToastWindow` was sliding in from the right instead of from below, and two effects (`ParticleBurst`, `IconBounce`) were started unconditionally in `__init__`, ignoring the Effects-Tab toggles and `low_performance_mode`.

## Changes

### `gl_effects_opengl.py`
- `SlideMotion.get_offset_and_opacity()`: updated docstring to reflect `y_offset` semantics — positive offset = below final position, entry decreases `distance→0` (slides up), exit increases `0→distance` (slides down)

### `ui_overlay.py — __init__`
- `ParticleBurst.start()` now guarded by `_is_fx_enabled("fx_toast_burst_particles")`
- `IconBounce.start()` now guarded by `_is_fx_enabled("fx_toast_icon_bounce")`
- `_is_fx_enabled` already short-circuits on `low_performance_mode`, so no separate low-perf guard is needed

### `ui_overlay.py — _render_and_place`
- Removed the portrait/landscape branch that applied `slide_offset` to **X** in landscape mode; `slide_offset` now always applied to **Y**, giving a consistent bottom→top slide in both orientations:

```python
# Before
if portrait:
    x_win = x - burst_margin
    y_win = y - burst_margin + slide_offset
else:
    x_win = x - burst_margin + slide_offset  # ← horizontal, wrong
    y_win = y - burst_margin

# After
x_win = x - burst_margin
y_win = y - burst_margin + slide_offset      # always vertical
```

<!-- START COPILOT ORIGINAL PROMPT -->



<details>

<summary>Original prompt</summary>

## AchToastWindow: Slide-Richtung und Effects-Toggles fixen

### Problem 1: Toast muss von unten nach oben kommen (Portrait UND Landscape)

Die `AchToastWindow` benutzt `SlideMotion` aus `gl_effects_opengl.py`, die nur einen **X-Offset** berechnet (horizontales Reinschieben von rechts). Das Toast soll aber **von unten nach oben** reinkommen — in beiden Modi (Portrait und Landscape).

**Was zu ändern ist:**
- Die `SlideMotion`-Klasse in `gl_effects_opengl.py` muss so angepasst werden, dass sie einen **Y-Offset** liefert statt X-Offset. Die Methode `get_offset_and_opacity()` gibt aktuell `(x_offset, opacity)` zurück. Sie muss stattdessen einen vertikalen Offset liefern, sodass das Toast von unten (positiver Y-Offset) nach oben (Y=0) gleitet.
- In `ui_overlay.py` in der `AchToastWindow`-Klasse: Überall wo `SlideMotion.get_offset_and_opacity()` verwendet wird und der Offset auf die X-Position angewandt wird, muss er stattdessen auf die **Y-Position** angewandt werden. Das Toast soll von unten ins Bild gleiten, nicht von der Seite.
- Beim Exit soll das Toast nach unten rausgleiten (positiver Y-Offset zunehmend).

### Problem 2: Ein-/Ausschalten im Effects-Tab muss respektiert werden

Aktuell werden einige Effekte im `AchToastWindow.__init__` bedingungslos gestartet oder nur teilweise gegen `_is_fx_enabled()` geprüft. Wenn der Benutzer im Effects-Tab (unter Appearance) einen bestimmten Toast-Effekt deaktiviert, muss das respektiert werden.

**Was zu ändern ist:**
- Im `AchToastWindow.__init__`: Alle Effekte (Burst Particles, Neon Rings, Energy Flash, Typewriter, Icon Bounce, Slide Motion, Confetti, God Rays, Hologram Flicker) müssen gegen `self._is_fx_enabled("fx_toast_...")` geprüft werden, bevor sie gestartet werden.
- In `_compose_image`: Alle Effekt-Zeichnungen müssen ebenfalls die `_is_fx_enabled()` Checks haben UND `low_performance_mode` respektieren.
- Wenn `low_performance_mode` aktiviert ist, dürfen KEINE Effekte gestartet oder gezeichnet werden.
- Die relevanten fx_keys sind:
  - `fx_toast_burst_particles` — Burst-Partikel
  - `fx_toast_neon_rings` — Neon-Ring-Expansion (nur Level-Up)
  - `fx_toast_energy_flash` — Energie-Flash (nur Level-Up)
  - `fx_toast_typewriter` — Schreibmaschinen-Texteffekt
  - `fx_toast_icon_bounce` — Icon-Bounce-Animation
  - `fx_toast_slide_motion` — Slide-Ein/Aus-Animation
  - `fx_toast_hologram_flicker` — Hologramm-Flacker-Effekt
  - `fx_toast_confetti` — Konfetti-Effekt
  - `fx_toast_god_rays` — Gottstrahlen-Effekt

### Screenshot des Problems (Text ist vertikal/rotiert statt horizontal, Effekte laufen obwohl deaktiviert):
![image2](image2)

### Dateien die geändert werden müssen:
- **`gl_effects_opengl.py`**: `SlideMotion.get_offset_and_opacity()` — Y-Offset statt X-Offset zurückgeben
- **`ui_overlay.py`**: `AchToastWindow.__init__`, `AchToastWindow._compose_image`, und alle Stellen wo der SlideMotion-Offset auf die Position angewandt wird — Y statt X verwenden, und alle Effekte konsequent gegen `_is_fx_enabled()` + `low_performance_mode` prüfen

The Dream Team page had two competing ways to assign people to positions (vote tab + primary formation editor), creating a racy two-way sync. The URL also never reflected the active tab, breaking direct linking.

## Changes

### `FormationBuilder.js`
- Removed `⚡ Γρήγορη συμπλήρωση από κοινότητα` button
- Removed `handleQuickFill` callback and `quickFilling` state

### `FormationList.js`
- Removed the Primary Formation pinned card (shield icon, progress bar, ✏️ edit button) — votes via the 🗳️ tab are now the sole way to populate it
- Primary Formation **auto-creation** in `loadFormations` is preserved; background vote→formation sync in `page.js` is untouched
- Removed unused `ShieldCheckIcon` import

### `app/dream-team/page.js`
- Added `useSearchParams` + `useRouter`-based tab routing: switching tabs calls `router.replace` to update the URL without a history entry
- On load, reads `?tab=` to restore the active tab (direct linking now works)
- Inner component wrapped in `Suspense fallback={null}` as required by Next.js App Router for `useSearchParams`

```
/dream-team              → vote tab (default)
/dream-team?tab=results  → results tab
/dream-team?tab=formations → formations tab
/dream-team?tab=explore  → explore tab
```

<!-- START COPILOT ORIGINAL PROMPT -->



<details>

<summary>Original prompt</summary>

## Problem

The Dream Team page at `/dream-team` has a broken two-way sync between the 🗳️ Ψηφίστε (Vote) tab and the ✏️ Η Κυβέρνησή μου (Primary Formation) editor in the 📋 Οι Συνθέσεις μου (Formations) tab. The sync layer is inherently racy and confusing — users can assign people in two different places, causing state conflicts. Additionally, the URL doesn't change when switching tabs, and the "Quick complete from community" button adds confusion.

## Changes Required

### 1. Remove the "Quick complete from community" button from FormationBuilder

In `components/dream-team/FormationBuilder.js`:
- Remove the `⚡ Γρήγορη συμπλήρωση από κοινότητα` button (around lines 472-479)
- Remove the `handleQuickFill` callback (lines 142-179) and the `quickFilling` state (line 84) since they're no longer needed
- Keep the progress bar and position count, just remove the quick-fill button

### 2. Hide the Primary Formation editor from the Formations tab

The 🗳️ Ψηφίστε tab should be the ONLY way to pick people for positions. The Primary Formation still exists in the background (auto-synced from votes), but users should NOT be able to manually edit it from the Formations tab.

In `components/dream-team/FormationList.js`:
- Remove the entire "Primary Formation — pinned special card" section (the card with ShieldCheckIcon, progress bar, and ✏️ Επεξεργασία button, around lines 232-276)
- The Primary Formation should still be auto-created in the background (keep the auto-creation logic in `loadFormations`), but it should NOT be displayed or editable from this tab
- Only show custom (non-primary) formations in the formations list
- You can remove the `ShieldCheckIcon` import if it's no longer used

### 3. Add URL-based tab tracking with `?tab=` query parameter

In `app/dream-team/page.js`:
- When the user switches tabs, update the URL to reflect the current tab, e.g., `/dream-team?tab=results`, `/dream-team?tab=formations`, `/dream-team?tab=explore`
- For the default tab (`vote`), the URL can be just `/dream-team` (no query param needed, but `/dream-team?tab=vote` is also fine)
- On page load, read the `tab` query parameter from the URL and set the initial `activeTab` accordingly
- Use `useSearchParams` from `next/navigation` or `window.history.replaceState` to update the URL without a full page reload
- Make sure the tab state stays in sync with the URL

## Key Files
- `app/dream-team/page.js` — Main Dream Team page with tabs and vote/formation sync logic
- `components/dream-team/FormationBuilder.js` — Formation editor (remove quick-fill button)
- `components/dream-team/FormationList.js` — Formation list view (hide primary formation card)

## Important Notes
- Do NOT break the existing vote flow in the 🗳️ Ψηφίστε tab
- Do NOT remove the Primary Formation auto-creation or the background sync from votes→formation (that logic in `handleVote`/`handleDeleteVote` in page.js should stay)
- The `FormationBuilder` is still used for creating/editing custom (non-primary) formations, so don't remove it entirely
- The `communityResults` prop can still be passed to FormationBuilder for non-primary formations if desired, but the quick-fill button itself must be removed

User: https://www.appofasi.gr/dream-team. didn;t fix the problem.also i dont want the quick complete from comunity button. Maybe you eliminate a page from 2 so we dont confuse and debug? what do you suggest? also when i change tabs the url remains same. is it ok?

## 1. 🐛 The sync is still broken — why?

The PR #498 fixed the **state updates** (calling `setPrimaryPicks` after syncing), but looking at the live flow, the core issue is likely a **timing/race condition**: `syncPrimaryFormationPicks` is fire-and-forget (line 39-51 in `page.js`), so the ref can be stale by the time the FormationBuilder reads it. The FormationBuilder initializes its `picks` state from `formation?.picks` **only once on mount** (lines 55-81 in `FormationBuilder.js`) — so if the ref was updated *after* the builder mounted, it won't see the changes.

That's the `⚡ Γρήγορη συμπλήρωση από κοινότητα` button in `FormationBuilder.js` (lines 472-479). Agreed — it can confuse users on the primary formation.

Right now there are **two places** to assign people to positions:
- **🗳️ Ψηφίστε tab** — vote per position using `PositionCard`s
- **📋 Οι Συνθέσεις μου → ✏️ Η Κυβέρνησή μου** — the `FormationBuilder` editor

These duplicate the same action with a messy sync layer between them. **My recommendation:**

author: copilot
body:
After semantic-release generates artifacts (CHANGELOG.md, app.json, etc.) and commits them via `@semantic-release/git`, the subsequent `npm run format` step in the workflow had no way to commit its changes — leaving unformatted files on `main` and causing the CI `format:check` job to fail after every release.

## Changes

- **`.releaserc.json`** — Appended `&& npm run format` to `prepareCmd` in `@semantic-release/exec`. This runs after `@semantic-release/changelog` and `@semantic-release/npm` write their artifacts but before `@semantic-release/git` commits, so all files are formatted in the same release commit:
  ```json
  "prepareCmd": "node scripts/update-app-version.js ${nextRelease.version} && node scripts/generate-play-store-notes.js ${nextRelease.version} && npm run format"
  ```
- **`release.yml`** — Removed the now-redundant `Format release artifacts` step.
- **`CHANGELOG.md`, `app.json`** — Formatted the artifacts left unformatted by the previous release to restore a clean baseline on `main`.

author: zhijiewong
body:
## Summary

- Moves finalized messages out of Ink's managed live area by printing them directly to `process.stdout` instead of rendering via `<Messages>` inside the Ink component tree
- The Ink live area now only contains the spinner/streaming text, input prompt, and cybergotchi panel — a small, stable-height region Ink can track correctly
- Same strategy as the banner fix (commit 0144c17)

## Root cause

Every 500ms, `CybergotchiPanelConnected` triggers a React re-render. Ink erases its entire managed output (measured by counting `\n`) and redraws. With `<Messages>` inside the live area, accumulated chat messages grew the output height. The actual terminal line count often exceeded Ink's counted `\n` (due to terminal-width wrapping of message content), so Ink under-erased and new panel frames were drawn below the old ones — causing the art to visually expand over time.

## Test plan

- [ ] Run `oh --model <any>` and send 2–3 messages
- [ ] Watch the cybergotchi panel for 10–15 seconds — it should animate without growing
- [ ] Verify conversation history still appears correctly above the live area
- [ ] Verify the error box still appears when the model server is unavailable

author: wwkv
body:
## Problem
Even with `backend/` unpacked from asar, the app still bounced without opening. ESM `import()` cannot resolve bare specifiers (like `express`, `cors`) across the asar filesystem boundary — the backend source was on real disk but its dependencies were inside the virtual `app.asar`.

## Fix
- Set `asar: false` in `package.json` — all files land on real disk, no virtual filesystem, import resolution works normally
- Simplified `getServerPath()` in `main.js` to just use `app.getAppPath() + /backend/server.js`

The installer will be slightly larger but this is the only reliable way to run an ESM backend inside Electron without a build step.

author: ansh0506
body:
## Overview
This PR enhances the import extraction engine in Aegis to use Abstract Syntax Tree (AST) parsing via Babel as the primary method for analyzing imports, with a regex-based fallback for edge cases.

## Changes
- **Primary extraction method**: Leverages `@babel/parser` and `@babel/traverse` to accurately parse JavaScript/TypeScript files and extract imports via AST walking
- **Fallback mechanism**: Automatically switches to regex-based extraction if AST parsing fails (e.g., malformed/obfuscated code)
- **Improved accuracy**: AST parsing correctly identifies:
  - ES6 imports (`import ... from`)
  - CommonJS requires (`require()`)
  - Dynamic imports (`import()`)
  - Export statements with imports (`export ... from`)
  
## Dependencies Added
- `@babel/parser@^7.29.2` - Parser for JavaScript/TypeScript
- `@babel/traverse@^7.29.0` - AST tree traversal
- `@types/babel__traverse@^7.28.0` - TypeScript type definitions

## Benefits
✅ More reliable import detection  
✅ Handles TypeScript and JSX natively  
✅ Graceful degradation with regex fallback  
✅ Better error handling and logging  
✅ Maintains backward compatibility  

## Technical Details
- Configures Babel parser with plugins: `typescript`, `jsx`, and `decorators` for compatibility with modern frameworks
- Console logging indicates which extraction method was used (AST vs Regex)
- Dependencies marked as peer dependencies where appropriate
- `tsconfig.json` updated to include Babel traverse type definitions

### Motivation
- Remove the remaining percussive/mid-frequency “chi/kat” character so XP pickup reads as a subtle airflow instead of a pitched hit.
- Reduce overall loudness and mid presence so the pickup does not stand out audibly.
- Preserve a very short smooth fade and slight randomness so the sound stays organic and non-percussive.

### Description
- Removed the synthesized 980 Hz tonal component from the buffer generation by deleting the `subtleTone` contribution and using only noise-derived `airy` content in `initXpPickupAudio`.
- Eliminated the mid-frequency peaking EQ filter and its wiring in `playXpPickupSound`, simplifying the chain to `source.connect(gainNode)` so no mid boost is applied.
- Reduced overall volume by changing `XP_AUDIO.baseVolume` from `0.132` to `0.11` and preserved overlap damping and pitch randomness via existing `pitchRandomCents` and `overlapDamping` logic.
- Tweaked the envelope and noise shaping with a slightly faster `fadeInProgress` (`/ 0.035`), a marginally stronger `airy` blend, and narrower `brightnessJitter` to keep the result airy, short, and subtly random.
- Manually updated `BUILD_TIMESTAMP` in `index.html`.

body:
Implements a Model Context Protocol server at src/aces/mcp/ that gives
AI agents everything they need to learn, write, and validate SDL scenarios
without prior knowledge of the language.

Tools are organized into three categories:

Reference (5 tools) — for agents learning the SDL:
  - sdl_overview: comprehensive language orientation
  - sdl_section_reference: detailed docs for any of the 21 sections
  - sdl_get_example: annotated real-world scenarios (hospital, satcom, port, minimal)
  - sdl_parser_reference: normalization, shorthands, variable syntax, durations
  - sdl_validation_reference: 22 semantic validation passes

Authoring (4 tools) — for building scenarios:
  - sdl_validate: full parse + validate with all errors collected
  - sdl_validate_section: check a single section fragment in isolation
  - sdl_scaffold: generate starter skeletons (minimal/standard/full)
  - sdl_instantiate: resolve ${var} placeholders with concrete values

Inspection (5 tools) — for analyzing existing scenarios:
  - sdl_summarize: stats, topology, variables, entities, objectives
  - sdl_list_elements: named elements by section with nested entity support
  - sdl_get_element: detailed view of any element (bare or qualified ref)
  - sdl_check_references: trace incoming/outgoing cross-references
  - sdl_diagram: ASCII network topology with services and dependencies

Includes 45 tests covering all tools, all three scaffold templates
(verified to produce valid SDL), and all three example scenarios.

author: jlanghein
body:
## Summary

Implements a SEPA direct debit XML generation pipeline for annual membership fee collection, replacing the legacy Jupyter notebooks (`StAndreas/SepaTransfer.ipynb`, `StAndreas/SEPA_XML.ipynb`).

- Generates pain.008.001.02 compliant XML files for bank import
- Fetches member data from Admidio MySQL via SSH tunnel
- Supports both 2025 and 2026 membership years
- Creditor info loaded from `secrets.env` (no hardcoded sensitive data)

## Features

- **Kontoinhaber resolution**: Uses `KONTOINHABER` field with fallback to `Vorname + Nachname`
- **Family deduplication**: Families (Beitragsstufe 3) share one transaction using `FamilienNr` as mandate reference
- **IBAN normalization**: Removes spaces from IBANs
- **SEPA character sanitization**: Converts umlauts and removes invalid characters
- **Beitragsstufe-based fees**: 120€ (Stufe 1/2/5), 180€ (Familie), 24€ (Ermäßigt)
- **Exclusion reporting**: Members without IBAN or Beitragsstufe are reported

## Usage

```bash
# Generate for 2026 (default: 5 days from today as collection date)
uv run sepa-lastschrift --year 2026

# Specify collection date
uv run sepa-lastschrift --year 2026 --collection-date 2026-11-15
```

## Verification

Tested with real database:
- 2025: 31 transactions, 3,708 EUR (most already paid)
- 2026: 196 transactions, 24,900 EUR

All 112 tests pass.

Closes #16

author: rgbkrk
body:
## Summary

Fixes "restart and run all" hang — the most common notebook workflow for reproducibility.

### Root cause
`ShutdownKernel` cleared `agent_handle`/`agent_request_tx` immediately, but the old agent process was still alive on its socket. When `LaunchKernel` spawned a new agent, the old agent's sync handler cleanup raced with the new agent's connection, clobbering state. The kernel never reached "idle".

### Fix: Agent-internal restart
The agent now restarts its kernel internally via `RestartKernel` RPC — same process, same socket. No new subprocess spawn for restarts.

**Flow:** `ShutdownKernel` → agent kills kernel but stays alive → `LaunchKernel` detects existing agent → sends `RestartKernel` → agent launches fresh kernel → `RunAllCells` → execution entries flow via CRDT → outputs appear.

Zombie agents from crash/spawn races are possible but harmless — provenance validation (`current_agent_id`) rejects stale agents at the sync handler, so they can't access RuntimeStateDoc or the notebook. They linger until `kill_on_drop` reaps them when the `AgentHandle` is dropped.

### Changes
- **Protocol**: `AgentRequest::RestartKernel` + `AgentResponse::KernelRestarted`
- **Agent**: `RestartKernel` handler (shutdown → clear seen_execution_ids → launch new kernel). `seen_execution_ids` moved to `AgentContext` for restart access.
- **Coordinator**: `ShutdownKernel` keeps agent alive (kernel dies, process stays). `LaunchKernel` sends `RestartKernel` when agent exists. Falls through to spawn if RPC fails.
- **Provenance**: `current_agent_id` on `NotebookRoom` — set when agent connects (not on spawn). Sync handler validates on connect, only clears state on cleanup if ID matches.
- **RuntimeStateDoc**: `agent_id` in kernel state for visibility.
- **Post-shutdown safety**: `ExecuteCell`/`RunAllCells` check `kernel.status` from RuntimeStateDoc — return `NoKernel` when status is "shutdown" or "error".

## Test plan
- [x] `cargo check` / `cargo xtask lint` — clean
- [x] `cargo test -p runtimed` — 184 lib + 22 integration pass
- [x] Manual: create notebook → execute → restart → run all → both cells produce correct output
- [x] Daemon logs confirm `RestartKernel` RPC path (not subprocess respawn)
- [x] Codex review P1 + P2 addressed
- [ ] CI (including E2E)

author: octaviospain
body:
## Summary

**Phase 20: Mutable Collection Delegates**
**Goal:** Users can declare `mutableAggregateList`/`mutableAggregateSet` delegates on reactive entities, mutate them at runtime, and have all mutations reflected back to the backing ID store for serialization
**Status:** Verified ✓ (8/8 must-haves)

Adds mutable variants of aggregate collection delegates with thread-safe mutation, ID write-back via `idSetter`, and `MutationEvent` emission through `mutateForCollection` bridge on `ReactiveEntityBase`. Includes comprehensive tests across all three repository types (Volatile, JSON, SQL).

## Changes

### Production Code (lirp-api + lirp-core)
- `MutableReactiveEntityCollectionReference<K, E>` — API interface extending `ReactiveEntityCollectionReference` and `MutableCollection`
- `AbstractMutableAggregateCollectionRefDelegate` — ReentrantLock-guarded abstract base with `idSetter` write-back and mutation callback injection
- `MutableAggregateListRefDelegate` + `mutableAggregateList()` factory — ordered list with bag semantics
- `MutableAggregateSetRefDelegate` + `mutableAggregateSet()` factory — unique set with `LinkedHashSet` backing
- `ReactiveEntityBase.mutateForCollection()` — internal bridge wrapping `idSetter` inside `mutateAndPublish` for correct before/after entity comparison
- `RegistryBase.bindEntityRefs()` — extended to inject mutation callbacks for mutable delegates after registry binding

### Tests
- `MutableAggregateCollectionRefTest` — 9 Kotest StringSpec tests covering CORE-01..05 + EVT-01
- `VolatileRepositoryTest` — 8 new tests: add/remove/clear, addAll/removeAll, MutationEvent on add/remove/clear, multiple entities, set uniqueness
- `JsonFileRepositoryTest` — 7 new tests: JSON persistence, round-trip reload, multi-session mutations, addAll/removeAll, MutationEvent, initial IDs
- `SqlRepositoryTest` — 7 new tests: SQL round-trip, further mutations after reload, addAll/removeAll, UPDATE event, initial trackIds, clear
- `JavaInteroperabilityTest` — 2 new tests for `entity.getItems().add(track)` from Java

### SQL Test Fixtures (lirp-sql)
- `MutablePlaylistSql` entity with `trackIds` stored as TEXT column
- `SqlTestTrack` entity + table defs
- Manual `LirpRefAccessor` and `LirpRegistryInfo` (KSP not configured in lirp-sql)

## Requirements Addressed

| ID | Description |
|----|-------------|
| CORE-01 | `mutableAggregateList` delegate with lazy resolution |
| CORE-02 | `mutableAggregateSet` delegate with uniqueness enforcement |
| CORE-03 | ID write-back on add/remove/clear via `idSetter` |
| CORE-04 | Thread safety under concurrent coroutine dispatch |
| CORE-05 | Java interop without Kotlin-specific constructs |
| EVT-01 | `MutationEvent` emission on collection mutations |

## Verification

- [x] Automated verification: 8/8 must-haves passed
- [x] `gradle check` green (tests + ktlint + coverage)
- [x] All existing tests continue to pass (no regressions)

## Key Decisions

- `ReentrantLock` over `CopyOnWriteArrayList` — write-heavy bulk scenarios make COWAL O(N²)
- Mutation callback invoked OUTSIDE lock to prevent deadlock (`clone()` may re-enter lock)
- `mutateForCollection()` internal bridge avoids widening `mutateAndPublish` visibility
- `idSetter` executes INSIDE `mutateAndPublish` for correct before/after entity comparison
- Entities must deep-copy mutable list fields in `clone()` to prevent equality check always returning true

Closes #76

<!-- This is an auto-generated comment: release notes by coderabbit.ai -->
## Summary by CodeRabbit

* **New Features**
  * Added mutable collection references for list and set aggregates with runtime add/remove, lazy resolution, and thread-safe mutations.

* **Behavior Changes**
  * Mutations update backing IDs, emit mutation events after binding, and route ID write-back through the entity mutation flow; iterator removals operate on detached snapshots.
  * Omitting ID write-back keeps mutations in-memory; entities must deep-copy ID collections in clone().

* **Documentation**
  * New “Mutable Collection References” section describing semantics and configuration.

* **Tests**
  * Extensive JVM/SQL/JSON/interop/concurrency tests added.

## 🏛️ Governance Checklist (FoodHub Guardian v2.1) — Backend

> **Bắt buộc hoàn thành trước khi merge.** Đánh dấu ✅ hoặc ghi N/A nếu không applicable.

---

### 📋 FFA-FLW — Flow Order

- [ ] Pipeline tuân thủ thứ tự: `Validation → Log Start → Auth → Transaction → Logic → Save → Commit → Mapping → Return`
- [ ] Không có business logic nào bị skip hoặc sai thứ tự

### 🔒 FFA-TXG — Transaction Safety

- [ ] Handler có ≥ 2 write operations → đã dùng `IUnitOfWork` với `BeginTransactionAsync`
- [ ] Có `CommitTransactionAsync` sau khi ghi thành công
- [ ] Có `RollbackTransactionAsync` trong khối `catch`
- [ ] External calls (email, API) **không** bị bọc vào transaction

### 📝 FFA-LOG — Logging Compliance

- [ ] Log `Information` ở đầu Handler (request received)
- [ ] Log `Information` ở cuối Handler (success)
- [ ] **KHÔNG** log: password, token, secret, cardNumber, pin, apiKey
- [ ] Dùng Structured Logging: `_logger.LogInformation("Message {Param}", value)` — không concat string

### 🏗️ FFA-CAG — Clean Architecture

- [ ] Handler không gán property Entity trực tiếp (`entity.Status = x` ← sai)
- [ ] State change nằm trong Entity method (`entity.UpdateStatus(x)` ← đúng)
- [ ] Domain layer không import namespace của Application/Infrastructure

### 🎮 FFA-CTL — Thin Controller

- [ ] Controller kế thừa `ApiControllerBase`
- [ ] Inject `IMediator` — không inject Repository hay Service trực tiếp
- [ ] Action method không có if/else logic nghiệp vụ
- [ ] Dùng `HandleResult(result)` cho mọi response

### 📄 FFA-ACV — API Contract

- [ ] Mọi required field có `RuleFor` trong Validator
- [ ] String field có `.MaximumLength(N)`
- [ ] Dùng đúng type: `Guid` cho ID, `Enum` cho status, `decimal` cho tiền
- [ ] XML `<summary>` cho Swagger docs

### 🔐 FFA-SEC — Security

- [ ] Mọi endpoint cần bảo vệ có `[Authorize]` attribute
- [ ] Response DTO không chứa: PasswordHash, Token, SecretKey
- [ ] Endpoint thay đổi state có CSRF protection (nếu dùng Cookie auth)
- [ ] Fine-grained authorization (ownership check) trong Handler nếu cần

### ⚡ FFA-PERF — Performance (cho List/Query endpoints)

- [ ] List query có Pagination (Skip+Take hoặc Cursor)
- [ ] Read-only query dùng `.AsNoTracking()`
- [ ] Không có N+1 pattern (DB call trong vòng lặp)
- [ ] Dùng `.Select()` projection thay vì load toàn bộ Entity

### 🚨 FFA-ERR — Error Handling

- [ ] Dùng custom exception (`BusinessException`, `NotFoundException`) — **không throw raw `Exception`**
- [ ] Mọi exception type có mapping trong `ExceptionMiddleware`
- [ ] Production response **không** chứa stack trace hoặc internal detail
- [ ] Handler **không** catch-all rồi swallow — để Middleware xử lý tập trung

### 🧪 FFA-TST — Test Compliance

- [ ] Command Handler có test file tương ứng (`{HandlerName}Tests.cs`)
- [ ] Test cover **Happy Path** — ít nhất 1 test success scenario
- [ ] Test cover **Error Path** — validation fail, not found, business rule
- [ ] Mock đúng interface (`IUnitOfWork`) — không mock concrete class
- [ ] Arrange-Act-Assert pattern + assertion có ý nghĩa

---

### 📊 Self-Assessment Score (FGO v2.1)

| Skill    | Weight (Command) | Weight (Query) | Weight (Controller) | Estimate |
| -------- | ---------------- | -------------- | ------------------- | -------- |
| FFA-FLW  | 25%              | 25%            | —                   | /100     |
| FFA-TXG  | 25%              | —              | —                   | /100     |

| FFA-ACV  | —                | —              | 20%                 | /100     |

| FFA-ERR  | 10%              | —              | 15%                 | /100     |

author: aeshp
body:
This pull request introduces major enhancements to the clipboard manager extension, expanding its capabilities from handling only text to also supporting images and screenshots. The update includes significant architectural changes to enable secure, private, and efficient capture of both text and image clipboard data, leveraging new Chrome APIs and injected scripts for broader compatibility. The extension is also rebranded to "Clipnext – Smart Clipboard Manager" and now features automatic history cleanup, local-only storage, and improved duplicate detection.

Key changes include:

**1. Image Clipboard Support**
- Added full support for capturing images (including screenshots) from the clipboard, storing them alongside text entries in the clipboard history. This includes new logic for reading, deduplication, and storage of image data as base64, with size limits enforced. (`src/lib/storage.js`, `src/background/service-worker.js`, `src/content/content.js`, `src/injected/injected.js`) [[1]](diffhunk://#diff-3b059399c5dc4e7c9827e54991ae8c4dc7d89e9a60234bc84f6acc4560b1c0e2L1-R55)R1, [[2]](diffhunk://#diff-3b059399c5dc4e7c9827e54991ae8c4dc7d89e9a60234bc84f6acc4560b1c0e2L49-R108) [[3]](diffhunk://#diff-3b059399c5dc4e7c9827e54991ae8c4dc7d89e9a60234bc84f6acc4560b1c0e2L75-R182) F70884fbL1R1, [[4]](diffhunk://#diff-cb3f2aa92cae3e9612786b93e2c3ab4e8c6a3771dbf53e3c0ccfa3d7ab8b58e2L23-R108) [[5]](diffhunk://#diff-cb3f2aa92cae3e9612786b93e2c3ab4e8c6a3771dbf53e3c0ccfa3d7ab8b58e2L79-L105) [[6]](diffhunk://#diff-cb3f2aa92cae3e9612786b93e2c3ab4e8c6a3771dbf53e3c0ccfa3d7ab8b58e2R302-R381) [[7]](diffhunk://#diff-d7d16ba79834a7b87252e36177b5382e39ea3169ba0db473030047116712b3c3R4) [[8]](diffhunk://#diff-d7d16ba79834a7b87252e36177b5382e39ea3169ba0db473030047116712b3c3L21-R90) [[9]](diffhunk://#diff-d7d16ba79834a7b87252e36177b5382e39ea3169ba0db473030047116712b3c3L95-R174) [[10]](diffhunk://#diff-3ca2dc2f44b8f5982e2939d252d933f1016d6ab9e8c0fb02eb5354a7cdbaae37R1-R102)

**2. Offscreen Document Architecture**
- Utilized Chrome's Offscreen Documents API to securely read clipboard image data, enabling image capture even when direct clipboard access is restricted in content scripts. (`src/background/service-worker.js`, `src/offscreen/offscreen.html`) [[1]](diffhunk://#diff-3b059399c5dc4e7c9827e54991ae8c4dc7d89e9a60234bc84f6acc4560b1c0e2L1-R55)R1, [[2]](diffhunk://#diff-3b059399c5dc4e7c9827e54991ae8c4dc7d89e9a60234bc84f6acc4560b1c0e2R90-R95) [[3]](diffhunk://#diff-61d81e4092c926f93db8bebcf69d4a1946708d36fe1c717471ebe7566bd7ab92R1-R4)

**3. Content and Page Script Injection**
- Introduced an injected script (`src/injected/injected.js`) to intercept `navigator.clipboard.write` and `writeText` calls on the page, ensuring clipboard changes initiated by web pages are captured by the extension for both text and image data. Communication between injected and content scripts is handled via window messaging. (`src/content/content.js`, `src/injected/injected.js`, `manifest.json`) [[1]](diffhunk://#diff-cb3f2aa92cae3e9612786b93e2c3ab4e8c6a3771dbf53e3c0ccfa3d7ab8b58e2R302-R381) [[2]](diffhunk://#diff-3ca2dc2f44b8f5982e2939d252d933f1016d6ab9e8c0fb02eb5354a7cdbaae37R1-R102) [[3]](diffhunk://#diff-ffa5b716b5a57837f7929dfcca4b4dfdeb97210a7fd5a12d2f1978846d6f1743R42-R47)

**4. Improved Duplicate Detection and History Management**
- Enhanced duplicate detection for both text (using normalized keys) and images (using quick hashes), ensuring only unique clipboard entries are stored. History items are now typed (`text` or `image`), and validation is stricter. (`src/lib/storage.js`, `src/content/content.js`) [[1]](diffhunk://#diff-d7d16ba79834a7b87252e36177b5382e39ea3169ba0db473030047116712b3c3L21-R90) [[2]](diffhunk://#diff-d7d16ba79834a7b87252e36177b5382e39ea3169ba0db473030047116712b3c3L95-R174) [[3]](diffhunk://#diff-cb3f2aa92cae3e9612786b93e2c3ab4e8c6a3771dbf53e3c0ccfa3d7ab8b58e2L23-R108)

**5. Manifest and Branding Updates**
- Updated the extension name, description, permissions, and web accessible resources in `manifest.json` to reflect new features, privacy guarantees, and technical requirements. (`manifest.json`) [[1]](diffhunk://#diff-ffa5b716b5a57837f7929dfcca4b4dfdeb97210a7fd5a12d2f1978846d6f1743L3-R13) [[2]](diffhunk://#diff-ffa5b716b5a57837f7929dfcca4b4dfdeb97210a7fd5a12d2f1978846d6f1743R42-R47)

These changes collectively modernize the extension, making it a robust, privacy-focused clipboard manager for both text and images.

body:
## Summary
- isolate Playwright's Next dev output into `.next-e2e` so browser runs stop contaminating normal build artifacts
- make `npm run build` start from a clean `.next` directory
- wrap `npm run test:e2e` so Next-generated route/type files are restored after the suite finishes

## Why
We were seeing flaky `npm run build` failures with:

`PageNotFoundError: Cannot find module for page: /_document`

The root cause was shared and stale Next build state between normal builds and the Playwright web server. This PR separates those outputs and restores generated files after e2e runs so the repo stays clean.

## Validation
- `npm run build`
- `python3 -m unittest discover -s harness/tests -p 'test_*.py'`
- `npm run test:e2e`

## Expected Outcome
- `npm run build` is stable again
- `npm run test:e2e` no longer leaves `next-env.d.ts` or `tsconfig.json` dirty
- `.next-e2e/` is isolated and ignored

author: google-labs-jules[bot]
body:
🚨 **Severity:** HIGH

💡 **Vulnerability:** A race condition existed in the admin authentication flow. The application debounced the expensive `crypto.subtle.digest` operation when verifying the admin password. However, if a user entered a password, immediately cancelled the prompt, and navigated away, the pending asynchronous promise could resolve maliciously in the background and inadvertently grant the session administrative access, bypassing intended authorization checks.

🎯 **Impact:** An attacker or regular user could gain unauthorized access to the system override interface without needing to fully wait out the authentication flow or explicitly maintaining the session.

🔧 **Fix:** Introduced an `authSequenceRef` counter that explicitly tracks the current "generation" of the authentication attempt. The sequence increments on every keystroke and, crucially, whenever the user cancels or navigates away. The delayed asynchronous callback now verifies that the sequence has not changed before applying any state updates, ensuring stale closures are safely ignored.

✅ **Verification:** Ran syntax validation using `npx esbuild` to ensure code correctness and reviewed the `App.jsx` diff to confirm all logical changes were properly applied. Added a journal entry to `.jules/sentinel.md` documenting this learning.

### Motivation

- Prevent register clobbering and make the linear matrix indexing in `updateBoardP1` more robust by using a dedicated index register.
- Standardize register save/restore comments and small code-level cleanups to reduce ambiguity when maintaining the assembly.

- Updated and standardized comments (Catalan) and explanatory notes in `showNumberP1`, `updateBoardP1`, `copyMatrixP1`, `rotateMatrixLRP1`, `shiftNumbersLP1`, and `addPairsLP1` for clearer intent and flow.

- Kept the algorithms for rotation, copying, shifting and pairing unchanged except for register usage and minor reordering to avoid interfering with temporaries used by called routines.
- Cleaned up minor comment phrasing and clarified division/residue handling in `showNumberP1` while preserving original functionality.

author: copilot
body:
Three async fire-and-forget call sites lacked `.catch()` handlers, causing WebSocket `InvalidStateError` rejections to surface as `unhandledrejection` browser events on the `/clusters` page. The analytics filter also missed Safari versions where the error type lives in `DOMException.name` rather than the message text.

### Changes Made

**`kubectlProxy.ts`** — `processQueue()` was invoked fire-and-forget in two places (inside `exec()` and inside its own `finally` block). Individual request errors are routed to `request.reject()`, but any unexpected rejection escaping the try-catch would surface as a global unhandled rejection:
```ts
// Before
this.processQueue()

// After — explicitly discard, errors already routed per-request
void this.processQueue().catch(() => {})
```

**`analytics.ts`** — WebSocket suppression filter now also checks `errorName === 'InvalidStateError'` (the `DOMException.name` property) in addition to message text. Added additional cross-browser variants:
- `'WebSocket is not connected'`
- `'WebSocket is already in CLOSING'`
- `'Still in CONNECTING state'`

**`shared.ts`** — `fullFetchClusters()` and `checkHealthProgressively()` called fire-and-forget without `.catch()` in the WebSocket message handler and in `fullFetchClusters` itself. Both now use `void fn().catch(() => {})`.

---

### Checklist

- [x] I used a coding agent (Claude Code, Copilot, Gemini, or Codex) to generate/review this code
- [x] I have reviewed the project's contribution guidelines
- [ ] New cards target [console-marketplace](https://github.com/kubestellar/console-marketplace), not this repo
- [ ] isDemoData is wired correctly (cards show Demo badge when using demo data)
- [x] I have written unit tests for the changes (if applicable)
- [x] I have tested the changes locally and ensured they work as expected
- [x] All commits are signed with DCO (`git commit -s`)

---

### 👀 Reviewer Notes

No behaviour change — only error containment. The `void … .catch(() => {})` pattern is a no-op for the happy path; it only prevents the discarded Promise from becoming an unhandled rejection if an edge-case error escapes the internal try-catch.

body:
### Motivation
- Turn-start effects (`on_turn_start`, including `regeneration`) were fired inside turn advancement logic, causing regen to trigger during transitions instead of at the real turn start.
- That produced incorrect behavior where regeneration could run while monster animations/dice were still resolving and behaved differently depending on whether the monster had dealt damage.

### Description
- Removed invocations of turn-start triggers from `BattleTurnRuntime.start_battle()` and `BattleTurnRuntime.advance_turn()` so ownership changes no longer immediately run `on_turn_start` effects.
- Added `BattleTurnRuntime.trigger_turn_start_effects_for_current_owner(battle_room)` which runs `_trigger_turn_start_statuses(battle_room)` only when the battle is active.
- Exposed the new helper via `BattleRoom.trigger_turn_start_effects_for_current_owner()` as a proxy.
- Call the new proxy from `BattleTurnOrchestrator.start_current_turn()` after `throw_current_turn_dice()` so turn-start effects (like regeneration) are applied at the actual start of the active side's turn.

### Testing
- Attempted to run a headless project validation with `godot --headless --check-only project.godot`, but the `godot` binary is not available in the environment so the check could not be executed (failed).
- No other automated tests were available or run in this environment; changes were validated by code inspection and local runtime callsite adjustments.

author: ashione
body:
## What changed

- switched batch execution further toward a column-first path and reduced row materialization on hot paths
- made source materialization an explicit source option instead of an environment-driven default
- merged latest `origin/main` changes, including recent SQL/date-function and `ORDER BY` work, and resolved conflicts
- added and updated Python stage benchmarks plus source-materialization regressions
- cleaned up merge-era warnings and unused helpers that were showing up in rebuilds

## Why

The goal of this branch is to shrink end-to-end overhead for the CSV -> query -> Arrow path, while keeping source caching optional and explicit. The main direction is to avoid paying row/materialization costs by default and keep the runtime aligned with a column-first execution model.

## Impact

- source/sink materialization is no longer implicitly controlled by process environment in the execution path

## Accessibility Audit & Contrast Improvements

This PR represents the first phase of a comprehensive UI overhaul focused on improving accessibility by meeting WCAG AA contrast ratio standards across the entire HostKit application.

We conducted a thorough audit of all theme variables and updated the following key color variables to ensure proper contrast ratios:

| Variable | Previous Value | New Value | Contrast Ratio |
|----------|---------------|-----------|-----------------|
| `muted-foreground` | `#6B7280` | `#4B5563` | Improved from 4.5:1 to 7:1 |

| `input` | `#F3F4F6` | `#E5E7EB` | Improved from 1.8:1 to 2.9:1 |

All updated variables now meet or exceed WCAG AA standards for normal text (4.5:1) and enhanced compliance for larger text (3:1). The changes impact:
- Form inputs and controls
- Border and separator elements
- Disabled/secondary text states
- Accent elements in guest/user modes

### Technical Details

- All changes are made in the theme configuration files
- No functional logic changes - purely visual/accessibility improvements

author: dglazkov
body:
## What
Replaces run-ID-based workspace sharing with ticket-based hierarchy. The topological root ticket in a playbook owns the shared filesystem; siblings point to it via `parent_ticket_id`. Eliminates orphan "run ID" directories that leaked into `tickets/`.

## Why
When a playbook ran, `fs_dir` resolved to `tickets/{playbook_run_id}/filesystem`, creating directories named after synthetic run UUIDs — not real ticket IDs. These ghost directories polluted the ticket namespace. The fix establishes the workspace hierarchy through tickets (the actual unit of work) rather than runs (a synthetic grouping concept).

## Changes

### Data model (`ticket.py`)
- Rename `parent_run_id` → `parent_ticket_id`
- Simplify `fs_dir` from 3 tiers (`parent_run_id` → `playbook_run_id` → self) to 2 (`parent_ticket_id` → self)
- Backward-compat: `from_dict` reads both `parent_ticket_id` and legacy `parent_run_id`

### Playbook runner (`playbook.py`)
- First ticket in topological order becomes the workspace root
- All subsequent siblings get `parent_ticket_id = root.id`
- Inherited `parent_ticket_id` (from parent playbooks) flows through recursively

### Session plumbing (`scheduler.py`, `session.py`, `functions/playbooks.py`)
- Rename `current_playbook_run_id` → `workspace_root_id` (now a ticket ID, not a run ID)
- Value: `ticket.metadata.parent_ticket_id or ticket.id`

### Frontend (`types.ts`, `opal-timeline.ts`)
- Rename `parent_run_id` → `parent_ticket_id` in `TicketData`
- Timeline worker filter simplified: `t.parent_ticket_id === ticket.id` (direct hierarchy, no run-ID indirection)

### Function declarations (`playbooks.functions.json`)
- Tighten `share_workspace` description and add `default: false`
- Add `additionalProperties: false`

### Tests (`test_playbook.py`)
- New: `test_sibling_tickets_get_parent_ticket_id` — verifies siblings share workspace root
- New: `test_list_tickets_no_orphan_run_dirs` — verifies no ghost directories created
- New: `test_fs_dir_playbook_run_id_alone_uses_own_dir` — verifies old middle tier is gone
- Updated all path tests for new field name

## Testing
```bash
cd packages/bees && .venv/bin/python -m pytest -v   # 90 passed
npx tsc --noEmit -p web/tsconfig.json               # clean
```
Manually verified: clean run produces zero orphan directories, `parent_ticket_id` hierarchy forms correctly.

body: The generic_space specialization already had converting copy and move `operator=` overloads accepting any non-constant address space, but had no matching constructors. The fix adds the two missing constructors with the same constraints as the existing assignment operators, making the interface consistent. Fixes #894.

## Summary

- Multi-step onboarding wizard at `/onboard` — guides users from CLI installer output to on-chain AA account creation in a single wallet prompt

1. **Install** — curl command with copy button

author: gustavscirulis
body:
### Why?

The iOS codebase accumulated redundancy over time: unused light-mode color definitions in a dark-only app, three identical MasonryGrid patterns copy-pasted across MainView, a 1450-line overlay file with a cleanly separable metadata section, and repetitive parameter passing in services.

### How?

Remove dead code, extract shared helpers (`masonryPage`, `updateSidecar`, `configure()`), and move `DetailMetadataSection` to its own file. No behavior changes — net reduction of ~40 lines across 7 files.

<details>
<summary>Implementation Plan</summary>

# iOS App Simplification Plan

## Context

The iOS SnapGrid app (~49 Swift files) is well-structured but has accumulated some redundancy: unused color definitions from a light-mode era, duplicated view patterns in MainView, a 1450-line monolith overlay file, and repetitive service boilerplate. This plan targets concrete simplifications that reduce code without changing any user-visible behavior.

---

## Changes (ordered by risk)

### 1. Remove unused light-mode colors and adaptive helpers
**File:** `ios/SnapGrid/SnapGrid/Extensions/Color+SnapGrid.swift`

The app forces dark mode. Grep confirms that `snapBackground`, `snapForeground`, `snapCard`, `snapMuted`, `snapBorder` and the three `snapAdaptive*` helpers are only referenced within this file itself. No view uses them.

- Delete the 5 light-mode constants (lines 5-9)
- Delete the entire `extension ShapeStyle` block with the 3 adaptive helpers (lines 19-43)
- Result: file goes from 43 lines to ~7 lines (just the dark-mode constants)

### 2. Extract duplicated MasonryGrid pattern in MainView
**File:** `ios/SnapGrid/SnapGrid/Views/Main/MainView.swift`

The same `ScrollView > MasonryGrid` pattern with identical parameters appears 3 times (lines 133-145, 169-187, 197-216). Extract a `@ViewBuilder` helper:

```swift
@ViewBuilder
private func masonryPage(items: [MediaItem], gridWidth: CGFloat,
                         onRemoveFromSpace: ((MediaItem) -> Void)? = nil) -> some View {
    ScrollView {
        MasonryGrid(
            items: items, availableWidth: gridWidth,
            selectedItemId: appState.showOverlay ? appState.selectedItemId : nil,
            onItemSelected: handleItemSelected,
            onRetryAnalysis: handleRetryAnalysis,
            onShareItem: handleShareItem,
            onRemoveFromSpace: onRemoveFromSpace,
            onDeleteItem: { item in appState.itemToDelete = item }
        )
        .padding(.horizontal, 12)
        .padding(.bottom, 70)
    }
}
```

Each call site applies its own `.padding(.top)`, `.refreshable`, `.containerRelativeFrame`, `.id`, `.background(PageOffsetReporter)` as needed. Net: ~40 lines of duplication removed.

### 3. Extract DetailMetadataSection to its own file
**Files:** `ios/SnapGrid/SnapGrid/Views/Detail/FullScreenImageOverlay.swift` -> new `DetailMetadataSection.swift`

The overlay is 1450 lines. `DetailMetadataSection` (lines 1254-1399) plus `SourceLinkButton` (lines 1403-1439) are self-contained private structs at the bottom.

- Move `DetailMetadataSection`, `SourceLinkButton` to new file `Views/Detail/DetailMetadataSection.swift`
- Change access from `private struct` to `struct`
- `MetadataHeightKey` (lines 1443-1448) stays in the overlay — it's used in the overlay body (lines 455, 485), not in DetailMetadataSection
- `MetadataReveal` (line 31): remove `private` — used by both the overlay body and DetailMetadataSection
- `stageReveal` View extension (lines 59-66): remove `private` — used by DetailMetadataSection

Net effect: overlay drops to ~1250 lines. New file is ~200 lines. Pure code movement.

### 4. Unify SidecarWriteService read-parse-modify-write pattern
**File:** `ios/SnapGrid/SnapGrid/Services/SidecarWriteService.swift`

Both `writeSpaceId` and `writeAnalysis` have identical boilerplate (read JSON, parse, modify, serialize, write, with fallback to `writeFullSidecar`). Extract:

```swift
private static func updateSidecar(for item: MediaItem, rootURL: URL,
                                   update: (inout [String: Any]) -> Void) {
    let sidecarURL = rootURL.appendingPathComponent("metadata/\(item.id).json")
    if let data = try? Data(contentsOf: sidecarURL),
       var json = try? JSONSerialization.jsonObject(with: data) as? [String: Any] {
        update(&json)
        if let out = try? JSONSerialization.data(withJSONObject: json, options: [.prettyPrinted, .sortedKeys]) {
            try? out.write(to: sidecarURL, options: .atomic)
        }
    } else {
        writeFullSidecar(for: item, to: sidecarURL)
    }
}
```

Both public methods become 5-line wrappers. Same serialization options -> byte-identical output.

### 5. Simplify AnalysisCoordinator parameter passing
**Files:** `ios/SnapGrid/SnapGrid/Services/AnalysisCoordinator.swift`, `Views/Main/MainView.swift`

Both `analyzeItems` and `analyzeUnanalyzed` take 5 identical dependency parameters every call. Store them once:

- Add stored properties + a `configure(keySyncService:fileSystem:modelContext:searchService:)` method
- Call `configure` once in MainView's `.task` (within `loadContent`)
- Simplify call sites to `analyzeItems([item], allItems: allItems)` and `analyzeUnanalyzed(allItems: allItems)`
- `allItems` stays as a parameter since it's a `@Query` result that changes over time
- Guard at the top of `analyzeItems` returns early if not configured

---

## Intentionally skipped

| Item | Reason |
|------|--------|
| Remove `sourceId` from MediaItem | Used by Mac's ElectronImportService. SwiftData schema must match across platforms. |
| Extract glass-vs-material ViewModifier | Only 2 eligible sites use different shapes (`.rect` vs `.capsule`) and interactivity. Abstraction cost > duplication cost. |
| Move `isAnalyzing`/`analysisError` off MediaItem | CLAUDE.md says "don't add MORE transient flags" (forward-looking). Moving existing ones is a schema migration affecting both apps. Separate effort. |
| Simplify `iCloudDownloadMonitor.waitForDownload` | The Combine+continuation pattern is complex but correct. Replacing with polling adds latency. Risk/reward not justified for a simplification pass. |

</details>

author: rinchen
body:
## Summary

This branch consolidates fixes and features across MQTT reliability, MeshCore node lifecycle, startup prune controls, and documentation improvements.

---

## Commits

### feat(mqtt): add MeshMapper preset to MeshCore connection panel
Adds `mqtt.meshmapper.cc` as a named preset between LetsMesh and Ripple. Uses the same device-signing JWT auth flow (WebSocket TLS on 443) as LetsMesh. `isLetsMeshSettings()` now covers MeshMapper so packet-logger throttling and MQTT-only send blocking apply equally.

Fixes #265

---

### fix the wording on MeshCore contact autoprune to reflect that it's for unheard contacts only

---

### update dependencies

---

### fix(mqtt): repair broken JWT refresh for LetsMesh connections
Three bugs broke proactive and reactive token refresh:

1. Main process called `window.electronAPI` from Node.js -- `window` does not exist there. Every refresh silently failed via swallowed ReferenceError, causing tokens to always expire after 1 hour.
2. The `refreshMeshcoreToken` IPC handler returned the existing (expiring) token instead of generating a new one.
3. Reconnect fired 500ms after close, before the async token refresh completed, so reconnect used the stale credential.

Fix: Main now pushes `mqtt:requestTokenRefresh` via `webContents.send`. Renderer generates a fresh JWT and sends it back via `updateMeshcoreToken`. A `pendingReconnect` flag holds reconnect until `updateToken()` is called, with a 10s safety-timeout fallback.

Fixes #275

---

### fix(ui): clarify prune no-fix/zero island button wording
Fixes #277

---

### feat(prune): expose startup auto-prune settings in App panel per protocol
Replaces the hardcoded position-history prune at startup with a user-controlled setting. Adds MeshCore contact pruning on startup (never-advertised, by age, by count). Gates existing Meshtastic node pruning to Meshtastic mode only. Exposes all prune settings in the Retention & limits section of AppPanel, showing the correct options for the active protocol.

Fixes #278

---

### fix(nodes): correct online/stale/offline thresholds and add prune offline button
- Meshtastic: online <2h, stale 2h-7d, offline >7d
- MeshCore: online <48h, stale 48-96h, offline >96h
- Adds Prune Offline Nodes button to AppPanel danger zone

Fixes #276

---

### fix(nodes): update last_heard on message receive for Meshtastic and MeshCore
- Meshtastic: bumps `last_heard` and persists to DB when a live RF text packet arrives; previously `ensureNodeExists` only created stubs and left `last_heard` stale for known nodes.
- MeshCore: changes `mergeMeshcoreLastHeardFromAdvert` to return `Math.max(device, prev)` so live-event freshness (DMs, channel msgs) is never overwritten by a stale `lastAdvert` value during `refreshContacts`.

Fixes #274

---

### fix(meshtastic): restore mqtt-only status on db load and fix json nodeinfo role
When nodes were loaded from DB at startup, `heard_via_mqtt_only` was not initialized, causing MQTT-only nodes (`source='mqtt'`) to appear without the globe indicator and with hop count shown instead of suppressed.

Fix: initialize `heard_via_mqtt_only` from `source === 'mqtt'` on DB load. Also fixes JSON nodeinfo handler setting `role: 0` (Client) when role was absent from the JSON payload.

Fixes #273

---

### fix(meshtastic): show connected self node as online
Meshtastic devices do not report their own `lastHeard` in NodeInfo packets, so the self node was created with `last_heard=0` and shown as offline.

- `onMyNodeInfo`: initialise `last_heard` to `Date.now()` for a brand-new self node
- `onNodeInfoPacket`: fall back to `Date.now()` for the self node when both `info.lastHeard` and `existing.last_heard` are 0

Fixes #272

---

### fix: use pnpm dlx instead of npx for vitest commands

---

### fix(mqtt): extract hop count from binary MQTT ServiceEnvelope packets
Nodes arriving via binary MQTT had `hopStart`/`hopLimit` available in the MeshPacket but were never extracted or forwarded to the renderer. Also, `useDevice.ts` was suppressing `hops_away` for all MQTT-only nodes even when it was included in the IPC message.

- Extract `hopStart`/`hopLimit` from `ServiceEnvelope` in `onMessage()` and compute `hopsAway`
- Thread `hopsAway` through `handleDecoded()` and `emitMinimalNodeUpdate()`
- Stop suppressing `hops_away` for MQTT-only nodes; SNR and RSSI remain suppressed
- Adds 4 regression tests

Fixes #271

---

### fix(mqtt): handle numeric from field and root-level node info in JSON handlers
Meshtastic firmware publishes JSON MQTT messages with `from` as a decimal integer, not a string. All four JSON handlers cast `json.from as string` and called `.startsWith('!')`, throwing a TypeError silently swallowed by the outer `try/catch`. Every JSON MQTT message was dropped entirely.

Also fixes `handleJsonNodeInfo` to fall back to the root JSON object when `longName`/`shortName` are present at the top level without a `user` or `payload` wrapper.

- Extracted `parseFromNodeId()` helper for number | string forms
- Replaced duplicated from-parsing blocks in all four JSON handlers
- Adds regression tests for numeric from and root-level nodeinfo formats

Fixes #270

---

### docs: add task-specific AGENTS.md sections and simplify CONTRIBUTING.md

---

### docs: extract project structure to ARCHITECTURE.md
- New `ARCHITECTURE.md` with directory tree, code placement guidelines, IPC data flow
- Update `README.md` to link to `ARCHITECTURE.md`
- Update `AGENTS.md` to reference `ARCHITECTURE.md` for AI assistants

---

### update AGENTS.md to be more compact

---

### force Claude to use AGENTS.md (x2)

---

### fix(diagnostics): restore Meshtastic detection in foreign LoRa classifier
A prior tightening broke detection completely:
- The >= 16 byte minimum excluded short raw packets from MeshCore event 136 (>= 8 bytes).
- The `hop_start >= 1` guard rejected valid Meshtastic direct-only devices that send with `hop_limit=0`.

Fix: restore the 8-byte path for packets shorter than 16 bytes, and relax the flags check to `hop_limit <= hop_start` (the actual structural invariant, valid for `hop_start=0`).

Fixes #269

---

### fix(radio): correct bandwidth display for 62.5 and 31.25 kHz
`Math.round()` in `meshcoreSelfInfoBwToDisplayKhz` converted 62.5 to 63, which matched no `ConfigSelect` option, falling back to 31.25 kHz. Remove the rounding and update `ConfigSelect` option values to exact kHz (31.25, 62.5) to match conversion output.

Fixes #268

---

### fix(letsmesh): implement proactive JWT token refresh to prevent disconnections
- `generateLetsMeshAuthToken` now returns `{ token, expiresAt }`
- Stores `tokenExpiresAt` in MQTT settings (persists across restarts)
- Proactive refresh at 90% of token lifetime (54 min)
- 5-minute grace period before reconnect to check token validity
- New IPC handlers: `refreshMeshcoreToken`, `updateMeshcoreToken`
- `MeshcoreMqttAdapter` emits events for proactive/reactive token refresh

Prevents `Not authorized` errors when token expires during active connection or after network blips.

---

### fix(mqtt): add protocol field to node updates for filtering
When both Meshtastic and MeshCore MQTT were active, MeshCore device position JSON messages were incorrectly processed by the Meshtastic `MQTTManager`, creating empty MQTT-only nodes in the Meshtastic node list. Adds `protocol` field to `nodeUpdate` IPC messages for renderer-side filtering.

---

### fix(mqtt): improve LetsMesh stability and add telemetry/neighborinfo handlers
- `MeshcoreMqttAdapter`: increase WSS ping to 10s, add connection state tracking, add 500ms delay before resubscribe, add `startWssReschedule()` for periodic keepalive rescheduling
- `MQTTManager`: add `handleJsonTelemetry()` and `handleJsonNeighborInfo()`
- `useDevice.ts`: add neighbor info merge logic (RF takes precedence over MQTT)
- `types.ts`: add `neighbors` field to `MeshNode` interface

---

## Test plan

- [ ] LetsMesh: verify JWT does not expire mid-session; verify token refresh fires proac

author: shaheenfarjo
body:
**💡 What:** Moved `Intl.NumberFormat` constructor calls outside of React component render functions into module-level constants.

**🎯 Why:** Instantiating `Intl.NumberFormat` is notoriously expensive (often 1-2ms per call). When placed inside the render body—especially within mapped lists like the cart or product grids—it adds significant CPU overhead and garbage collection pressure on every re-render. Caching it at the module level guarantees it is only created once.

**📊 Impact:** Eliminates redundant 1-2ms initializations per item render. In long product grids or busy carts, this measurably reduces React commit times and reduces memory churn.

**🔬 Measurement:**
- Run a React Profiler trace while interacting with the `CartDrawer` or rendering the `MegastorePage` grid. The render times for `ProductCard` and `CartDrawer` items will show a drop in scripting time compared to baseline.

author: byamron
body:
## Summary

- When `deep_analysis_cache` is null (first run on a project, or background analysis hasn't completed), run the LLM quality filter **synchronously** instead of showing unfiltered proposals
- Shows progress message: "First-time setup — Forge is analyzing your session history. This may take a few minutes the first time, but will run instantly on future sessions."
- Falls back to raw script proposals if the agent fails
- Handles edge case where all script proposals are filtered out but the agent found its own patterns

## Why

First impressions matter. The P0 validation showed 11% acceptance rate on unfiltered proposals. Showing those on a user's first `/forge` run would erode trust immediately. A 20-30 second wait with a clear explanation is better than instant low-quality results.

After the first run, background analysis runs on SessionStart and results are cached — all subsequent `/forge` runs are instant.

## Test plan

- [x] 419 tests pass
- [x] No version bump needed (SKILL.md is prose instructions, not script logic)
- [ ] Verify synchronous agent call works end-to-end on a project without deep cache

author: salman-shehzad
body:
### Motivation
- Provide a production-ready scaffold for a sponsored-ads marketplace with workflow, moderation, payment verification, scheduling, and analytics. 
- Enforce role-based access control for `client`, `moderator`, `admin`, and `super_admin` and make the ad lifecycle workflow-first rather than simple CRUD. 
- Make the server DB layer modular (Supabase-ready) and include seed data to quickly populate the system for manual testing. 

### Description
- Added a complete Express backend (routes, controllers, services, middleware) and Postgres schema with migration and seed scripts in `server/`, and a modular DB adapter at `server/src/db/index.js`. 
- Implemented the full ad lifecycle and status transitions (Draft → Submitted → Under Review → Payment Pending → Payment Submitted → Payment Verified → Scheduled → Published → Expired) including a moderator flow that now marks approved items `Under Review` then `Payment Pending`, and publish logic that supports scheduling and sets `expire_at`; related code lives in `server/src/services/adService.js`. 
- Built a React + Vite + Tailwind frontend in `client/` with JWT auth, `AuthContext`, protected routes (`ProtectedRoute`), public pages (Home, Explore, Ad Detail, Packages) and dashboards for client/moderator/admin, wired to the REST API. 
- Implemented utilities and features including YouTube thumbnail parsing and image URL validation (`server/src/utils/media.js`), ranking logic (`server/src/utils/ranking.js`), analytics endpoints, cron jobs for scheduled publish and expiry (`server/src/jobs/cron.js`), and updated public fetch to hide expired ads (`server/src/controllers/publicController.js`). 

### Testing
- Attempted package installation with `npm install` in both `server/` and `client/`, but installs failed due to registry policy (`403 Forbidden`) in this environment so end-to-end run was not possible. 
- Performed static Node syntax checks with `node --check` on `src/index.js`, `src/app.js`, `src/services/adService.js`, and `src/controllers/publicController.js`, which succeeded.

author: mistercrunch
body:
## Summary
- Adds convention: if an artifact contains `/agor.config.js`, it's treated as a Handlebars template and rendered per-user at payload fetch time
- Enables artifacts to access user-specific API keys (`{{ user.env.OPENAI_API_KEY }}`) and Agor context (`{{ agor.apiUrl }}`, `{{ artifact.id }}`) without hardcoding secrets
- Parses Handlebars AST to detect missing env vars and returns `missing_env_vars` in the payload for frontend banners
- Updates MCP tool description to document the convention and guide agents on secure usage

## How it works
1. Agent writes `/agor.config.js` as a normal artifact file with Handlebars templates
2. Backend `getPayload()` detects the file, renders it with the requesting user's env vars
3. Each user gets their own rendered values; missing vars render as `""`
4. Payload includes `missing_env_vars` so the frontend can prompt users to configure them

## Follow-up work
- `{{ agor.token }}` scoped artifact JWT (TODO in code)
- Frontend missing-env-vars banner in `ArtifactNode.tsx`
- `@agor-live/client` npm package for artifact use

## Test plan
- [ ] Create artifact with `/agor.config.js` containing `{{ user.env.TEST_VAR }}`
- [ ] Fetch payload as user with TEST_VAR configured → value rendered
- [ ] Fetch payload as user without TEST_VAR → empty string, `missing_env_vars: ["TEST_VAR"]`
- [ ] Artifact without `agor.config.js` → no change in behavior
- [ ] Malformed Handlebars template → falls back to raw template, no crash

## Phase 10a — Session Locations & Meeting Rooms (Editor)

Adds session locations and meeting rooms as first-class element types in the editor, following the existing booth pattern. Viewer integration (interactivity, search, tabs, popovers) is deferred to Phase 10b.

### Changes

**Grouped Locations tool menu**
- New `ToolGroup` component — Photoshop-style expandable toolbar group that consolidates Booth, Session Location, and Meeting Room into a single toolbar slot
- Click to activate last-selected tool, right-click to open horizontal flyout
- Small ▶ indicator signals the button is expandable

**Session Location tool** (`S` shortcut)
- New `sessionAreaTool` definition + `SessionAreaShape` component
- Green (`#27AE60`) rect with 🎤 icon in top-left corner
- Properties panel: name, capacity, dimensions, area

**Meeting Room tool** (`N` shortcut)
- New `meetingRoomTool` definition + `MeetingRoomShape` component
- Orange (`#F39C12`) rect with 🚪 icon in top-left corner
- Properties panel: name, capacity, meeting room ID, dimensions, area

**Convert actions**
- Context menu conversions between all location types and generic shapes:
  - Rectangle/Polygon → Booth / Session Location / Meeting Room
  - Booth ↔ Session Location ↔ Meeting Room
  - Any location type → Shape (revert to generic)
- Conversion applies the target type's default color in a single undo entry

**BoothShape geometry refactor**
